src:
MOV     AH, 62h          ; DOS: the PSP segment in BX
INT     21h
MOV     ES, BX           ; ES:0000 = the PSP
MOV     DX, OFFSET SAMEM1
MOV     AX, CS
CMP     AX, BX           ; in a .COM they are the same
JE      SAY1
MOV     DX, OFFSET OTHERM1
SAY1:
MOV     AH, 09h
INT     21h
MOV     DX, OFFSET FIRSTM1
MOV     AH, 09h
INT     21h
XOR     SI, SI
MOV     AX, ES:[SI]      ; the first two bytes: CDh, 20h
XCHG    AL, AH           ; in reading order
CALL    PHEX
MOV     DX, OFFSET INT20M1
MOV     AH, 09h
INT     21h
MOV     DX, OFFSET TAILM1
MOV     AH, 09h
INT     21h
MOV     AL, ES:[SI+80h]  ; the length of the command tail
MOV     AH, 0
CALL    PDEC
MOV     DX, OFFSET BYTESM1
MOV     AH, 09h
INT     21h
PUSH    CS
POP     ES

SAMEM1  DB      "PSP segment = CS", 13, 10, "$"
OTHERM1 DB      "PSP segment is not CS", 13, 10, "$"
FIRSTM1 DB      "PSP:0000 = $"
INT20M1 DB      " (INT 20h)", 13, 10, "$"
TAILM1  DB      "command tail: $"
BYTESM1 DB      " bytes", 13, 10, "$"
PHEX    PROC    NEAR     ; print AX as four hex digits (changes AX BX CX DX)
MOV     BX, AX
MOV     CX, 4
PHEX1:
PUSH    CX
MOV     CL, 4
ROL     BX, CL           ; the top digit to the bottom
POP     CX
MOV     DL, BL
AND     DL, 0Fh
ADD     DL, "0"
CMP     DL, "9"
JBE     PHEX2
ADD     DL, 7            ; "A" to "F"
PHEX2:
MOV     AH, 02h
INT     21h
LOOP    PHEX1
RET
PHEX    ENDP
PDEC    PROC    NEAR     ; print AX in decimal (changes AX BX CX DX)
MOV     BX, 10
XOR     CX, CX           ; digits on the stack
PDEC1:
XOR     DX, DX
DIV     BX               ; AX = AX / 10, DX = the last digit
PUSH    DX
INC     CX
OR      AX, AX
JNZ     PDEC1
PDEC2:
POP     DX               ; the digits come back first to last
ADD     DL, "0"
MOV     AH, 02h
INT     21h
LOOP    PDEC2
RET
PDEC    ENDP
